title: The file records that its own headline figure is not a measurement, and the figure was quoted anyway
detects: A result artefact whose `self_invalidated` field is set: the tool that wrote it recorded, at that moment, that the number inside is not a measurement of what it is named after. The field says which of two things happened. Either the verdict was read at a token position that did not hold it, so the AUC describes whatever was there instead, or a null ruler reading only a surface property of the prompts, their length or their character count, separated the two arms as well as the compass did. `docs/guide/compass.md` sets that second bar: if your AUC does not clear the length baseline, you have not measured anything.
incident: Ours, twice. 2026-09-26: a reader's first run printed `MARGIN_READOUT_SUSPECT ... THE AUC ABOVE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT OF HARM DISCRIMINATION`, exited 0, and this checker then said `nothing found` about the very file that run had just written. Two commands in one tool looked at one run and disagreed, and the one that reads like a verdict was wrong. 2026-09-27: two more readers, independently and on different hardware, quoted AUCs their own null controls had beaten, 0.8576 against a character-count ruler at 1.0000 and against a length ruler at 0.8993. This checker reported nothing found on those too, and on `evidence/compass-2026-07-30/base-qwen3-0.6b.json`, which this project's README calls "not a measurement of anything" for exactly that reason. The controls were computed, recorded and printed throughout. Nothing was wired to them.
remedy: Do not quote the figure. Read the `self_invalidated` field to see which fault it was. If the verdict was read at the wrong position, nothing is wrong with the model or the corpus: check what the run printed after `top=`, and for a thinking model pass a chat template that closes the reasoning block. If a null ruler won, the corpus is what failed: the two arms differ in something a ruler can see without understanding them, usually prompt length, so match them on it or score more rows.
false_positive: The field is written only when the producing tool has already decided its own figure is not a measurement, so a false positive here means the tool was wrong about itself rather than this check misreading it. An artefact that records nothing under the field is SKIPPED, not passed. Another harness with the same defect will not trip this, because the field is ours: that is a gap in coverage, not a clean bill of health. For artefacts written before the compass recorded the null comparison, the adapter works it out from the controls the file already carries. It compares distance from chance rather than the raw AUC, because a control at 0.0 separates the arms perfectly with its labels reversed, and it allows no tolerance, so a tie fires. A deliberately tiny run will trip this and be right to: a null ruler wins by chance on few rows, and the honest reading is that the run measured nothing either way.

fires_on.self_invalidated: the two verdict sets hold 10.49% of the probability
